name: @vanillagreen/pi-jev
description: A modular substrate for Jev/TypeSafe decisions in Pi: consumers queue or send question sets against a shared per-session core. Ships a deferring permission authorizer for @gotgenes/pi-permission-system and an intent-nudge consumer.

settings.label: Mode
settings.description: shadow records what the judge would decide and always defers to the permission prompt. live lets it auto-allow or refuse; @gotgenes/pi-permission-system still caps an allow on its own path surfaces.

settings.label: Authorizer link name
settings.description: The name to list in the permission system's authorizerChain. Registration alone grants no authority, so the link decides nothing until it is named there.

settings.label: Band edge
settings.description: Satisfied at p >= this value, violated at p <= 1 - it, unclear in between. Applies to every question until one has a measured threshold. Must be above 0.5.

settings.label: Advisory band edge
settings.description: Band edge for nudging questions. Lower than the veto edge because a wrong nudge costs a sentence while a wrong veto refuses work. Must be above 0.5.

settings.label: Judge model
settings.description: TypeSafe model name for every question. Recorded with each decision, because a threshold does not transfer between models.

settings.label: Judge timeout
settings.description: Milliseconds one Jev call may take before it is treated as a failure. This is time added ahead of the permission prompt, and a timeout defers to the human rather than deciding.

settings.label: Session request cap
settings.description: Attempts this judge may make in one session, including failed ones. Reaching it defers every later ask. Daily caps from PI_TYPESAFE_MAX_* still apply and can only lower this.

settings.label: State retention
settings.description: hash keeps only a state hash and the answers; full also keeps the state, which is what a replay calibration needs and what makes the log a record of conversation content.

settings.label: User messages in state
settings.description: How many of the user's own messages the judge is shown. 0 sends no intent at all, leaving the action to be judged on its own.

settings.label: Recent tool calls in state
settings.description: One line per tool call the agent already made, oldest first. Trimming drops these before it drops the user's instructions.

settings.label: Plan in state
settings.description: How much of the agent's own words before the call reach the judge. 0 removes the plan, which also removes the question that compares the call against it.

settings.label: Toolbox in state
settings.description: How many available tools, with a one-line description each, the judge sees. This is what lets it judge whether the agent reached for the right tool. 0 omits the question.

settings.label: State budget
settings.description: Character ceiling for one state. TypeSafe also caps a request at 64 KiB and 32 questions, which the pack stays well inside.

settings.label: Decision log
settings.description: JSONL file holding one ask record per evaluation and one decision record per permission resolution, joined by requestId. Empty uses <agent dir>/pi-jev/decisions.jsonl.

settings.label: Deliver nudges
settings.description: Send this package's veto findings to the agent as a steer. The intent consumer has its own switch.

settings.label: Deliver intent nudges
settings.description: Send the intent consumer's advisories to the agent as a steer: it names the question and the mismatch when a tool call contradicts the plan the agent just stated. Off until the report shows how often it would fire on your sessions.

settings.label: Queued-question wait
settings.description: How long a queued question may wait with no send before the core asks it anyway, in milliseconds. 0 disables the timer: queued questions are then answered by the next send, or at the turn boundary. A timed flush only runs mid-turn, and it is always late — it can nudge and log, never gate.
